title: The Mosquito Bowl producer recalls runaway parrot ordeal
excerpt:
Alex Gayner recalls a parrot escaping during filming in Australia.
The crew recovered the bird after hours of searching.
body_md:
Producer Alex Gayner has revealed an unexpected production challenge from The Mosquito Bowl, the historical drama directed by Peter Berg. Despite decades of experience working on large Hollywood productions, one of his most stressful moments on the movie involved an animal performing in a scene that ultimately occupied only about ten seconds of screen time.

Adapted from Buzz Bissinger's book, the film follows four real college football players who joined the United States Marine Corps during World War II. Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgard, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis appear in the drama. The cast underwent football training with assistance from experienced sports professionals, including Christian McCaffrey, before filming in Queensland, Australia.

Berg wanted to reproduce a personal detail from the life of Tony Butkovich, played by Nicholson. Historical photographs showed the former football player with a parrot on his shoulder, and the filmmaker wanted that detail represented using a real bird rather than a computer-generated substitute.

Finding a suitable animal in Australia required considerable preparation. The production arranged months of logistical planning and training, with Nicholson learning how to interact with the bird. When the scene was finally ready, the crew remained quiet so that the animal would not be unnecessarily startled.

Within seconds of the cameras rolling, however, the parrot flew into the surrounding forest and disappeared among the tall trees. The incident brought filming to a halt and left the animal handlers searching through dense vegetation. Berg worried about the possibility of harm coming to the bird, while Gayner remained hopeful that the team could recover it.

After several hours, the handlers successfully retrieved the parrot and the production obtained the footage it needed. The incident became an unusually memorable example of the unpredictable work involved in practical filmmaking.

Gayner and Berg had previously developed a shared preference for capturing physical environments and performances on camera while making American Primeval. Their collaboration continued with The Mosquito Bowl, and the pair are also working on a film adaptation of Call of Duty.

Before becoming a producer, Gayner worked as an assistant director on productions including Pacific Rim and Godzilla. His transition into producing included Nicolas Winding Refn's Too Old to Die Young and the first season of Beef, for which he earned an Emmy.

The Mosquito Bowl is now streaming on Netflix. Gayner's account offers a reminder that even a brief detail in a finished film can require extensive planning, specialized personnel and considerable patience when filmmakers choose practical methods.
